target_customer: Food enthusiasts who buy curated products and experiences from independent makers such as chefs, farmers and roasters
problem: Quality food products from small makers are hard to discover and often not shipped, so a personal curator finds, delivers and explains them.
business_model: Curated e-commerce marketplace selling maker products and exclusives, with a curator service
product_category: Curated food and culinary products discovery marketplace

founders.name: Alex Matsenov
education: Advanced degree in machine learning (institution not named)
founders.background_notes: From the YC page, which calls him a 3x founder (2x YC) and a late-stage venture investor in machine learning.

founders.name: Daniel Shein
founders.background_notes: YC page calls him a lifelong engineer turned restaurateur; no employers or education stated.

technical_complexity.rationale: An e-commerce and curation app with shipping coordination; the hard parts are sourcing and logistics, not technology.

defensibility.rationale: Relationships with makers across 40 countries are slow to build, but curated marketplaces are copyable.

market_need_then: Interest in artisan and chef driven food products and direct to maker buying was growing, and pandemic era online food buying rose in 2020 (not sourced for this company).

branding.domain_note: Uses onkaiten.com with an on prefix; kaiten.com history not found.

identity.visual_style: Editorial product pages with exclusives and limited editions
identity.voice_and_tone: Personal curator and community of chefs and makers

rebrands.why: Not stated; the legal entity is still Agnoris, Inc.

brand_strength.rationale: No press or community evidence found; the word also means conveyor belt sushi in Japanese and a project management tool uses the name, so it is confusable.

outcome_analysis: Kaiten joined YC in Winter 2020 as a food discovery app and is still operating in 2024 as a curated marketplace with a personal curator service. No press on funding, traction or exits exists, so its outcome cannot be judged. It appears to be a small, low profile business rather than a venture scale breakout.
notes: Only an aggregator (CB Insights) lists a 0.5M convertible note from YC dated January 2020, not cross-checked, so no round recorded. Competitors left empty: only a CB Insights comparison with Here Here Market (founded 2019) was found, undated. Formerly named Agnoris per CB Insights and altss, rebrand date unknown. Founding year and location conflict among aggregators.
